fullPassage:
Many crises today, such as the Great Recession, are simply too big and too overwhelming for you to completely comprehend, much less control. Crises of this ilk are precisely the kind that can easily engulf you with destructive reactions that interfere with your ability to overcome them. Focusing on these oversized crises will exacerbate the natural psychological, emotional, and physical reactions you are going to experience. With these sorts of crises, your best chance is to identify those aspects that are within your control. Then, you can break down the bigger crisis into smaller, more manageable problems toward which you can direct your energy and find solutions. For example, think back to the Great Recession. Although you probably didn’t have the ability to influence economic policy, you were able to revisit the distribution of your investments and choose to create a more diverse portfolio.

Consumer surveys indicate that the majority of Americans (91%) believe they have some control over their health, and 72% believe that food and nutrition play the greatest role. However, 75% of consumers rely on media outlets including the Internet as their major sources of health and nutrition information, and only half use medical sources. A Google search for “nutrition listservs” yielded over 100,000 sites, but it is likely that many of these writings are not reviewed by nutrition experts. Internet sites marketing herbs, drugs, and health devices are not monitored by government regulatory agencies and often contain misleading information. Reputable food companies provide helpful facts about the nutrient content of their products, but commercial sites devoted to sales often post misleading health claims. Internet sites maintained by government agencies, universities, state extension services, and medical facilities provide evidence-based information and should be the first source for public information on foods, nutrition, and health.

My business partner Charles and I embraced the servant leader’s way of doing things. In other words, nothing was beneath us. We led by example and did the work. When any new salesman came into the store, he would look around, notice Charles polishing some corner of the floor and me covered in flour, and assume the decision-maker was not present. He’d then hand off whatever he was selling to me and say, “Can you give this to the owner?” Now, if Charles and I had remained in the bakery for too long, we wouldn’t have been able to grow and scale, so I’m not saying you should be sweeping the floors forever. It’s more about modeling what’s important. If cleanliness and details are important, be sure you aren’t above doing the work and pitching in. Come into your workspace and ask how you can help. If it’s clear your team is in the weeds, jump in without asking.

Training and competition naturally speed the breath, which activates the sympathetic nervous system. In performance, this is acceptable because an athlete wants to produce adrenaline and compete in an aroused state. However, it is equally important for an athlete to learn how to mentally and physically downshift from the acute sympathetic activity experienced in sport, and outside of performance focus their attention on slow breathing to reduce the sympathetic activity and resolve the fight-or-flight state. In the Feinstein Institutes study, participants were able to use the pace of their breathing to activate specific regions of the brain. In a performance realm, this means athletes can use breathing pace to manage their state of arousal. During training and competition, the breathing rate increases with the introduction of adrenaline, and athletes must be able to control this to be able to adapt and recover. One way is to practice slower breathing protocols outside of training and competition.

The study of literature has repeatedly failed to recognize the influence of modern musical lyricists and their contributions to the evolution of language. Unlike Shakespeare, who has been studied and celebrated for his development of the English language, particularly in vocabulary and grammatical structure, modern songwriters have experienced restraints on the acknowledgement of their contributions and largely been ignored. Over the past century, we have witnessed an explosion of incredible literary works by these artists, who, through their music, have used linguistic manipulation and storytelling to enrich our language and literature. Producing lyrics of distinct and complex imagery, songwriters have had an incredible literary impact on our language. Their remarkable works, including influences on modern language development, must be recognized in the field of modern literature.

questions.passage: "Where could it be?" Sophie asked herself. It had been more than ten years since she had last visited the area where she had grown up. The village had changed a lot over time. ① Uncertain, she awkwardly looked around at her surroundings. She walked the narrow streets of the village, unsure about which way to go. ② Suddenly, Sophie saw a familiar sight. "Yes, this must be it," she thought. ③ Although the colors were now faded, the familiar shapes on the wall were the same ones she had painted with her father as a child. ④ Sophie nodded, smiled brightly, and walked toward the gate.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?
In front of her was a wall with flowers painted on it.

det.korean: "Yes, this must be it"이라고 생각한 직후, 그녀 앞에 꽃이 그려진 벽이 있었다는 문장이 와야 자연스러움. 그 다음 벽의 색이 바랜 것을 설명.
det.analysis:
✅③: "this must be it" 직후 → 꽃 벽 발견 → 색이 바랜 설명으로 연결
❌①: 아직 길을 찾는 중
❌②: 익숙한 광경을 보기 전
❌④: 이미 벽 설명 완료 후
det.tip: 대명사 "this must be it"이 가리키는 대상이 바로 뒤에 나와야 자연스러움

questions.passage: The organ, his most precious possession, was a source of comfort and joy, especially in these uncertain times. ① But his peace was interrupted by the distant roar of engines breaking the calm. ② Francis' heart raced; it was wartime, and soldiers often took what they wanted. ③ Whispering urgently to his sister, Ellen, he led her to hide behind a tall tree, its thick trunk shielding them. ④ Peeking out, Francis stepped outside carefully and looked at the soldiers walking toward their home.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

det.analysis:
✅②: 엔진 소리 → 군인 등장 → 심장이 뛰는 반응
❌①: 아직 평화가 깨지기 전
❌③: 이미 숨으려고 행동 중
❌④: 이미 밖으로 나와서 보는 중
det.tip: 사건 순서: 엔진 소리 → 군인 등장 → 공포 반응 → 숨기

questions.stem:
주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
down / my / on / pressing / mind

det.korean: press down on(~을 짓누르다) + my mind → "마음을 짓누르는" 비유 표현
det.analysis: pressing down on my mind: press down on(~을 짓누르다) + my mind(내 마음)
det.tip: press down on = ~을 짓누르다 / 무거운 돌이 마음을 짓누르는 비유

questions.passage: After a few nights, we ①<u>ventured</u> out on a hike to 16,000 feet. The group members were all ②<u>experienced</u>, so I couldn't understand why they were climbing so slowly. Having ③<u>trained</u> hard for this, I was in the best shape of my life. Then, as we ④<u>approached</u> 16,000 feet, I suddenly began to feel dizzy. Not long after, I was staggering. In a matter of minutes, I became a basket case, needing assistance just ⑤<u>walk</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: "needing assistance just to walk"에서 '걷기 위해'라는 목적의 to부정사가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
❌⑤walk: needing assistance just to walk → to부정사 필요
✅①ventured: 과거시제 동사
✅②experienced: 형용사(경험 많은)
✅③trained: 분사구문(Having trained)
✅④approached: 과거시제 동사
det.tip: need assistance to V = ~하기 위해 도움이 필요하다

questions.passage: Vera ①<u>couldn't</u> wait for her car to get fixed, but that was going to require longer than initially expected. Unfortunately, that meant ②<u>relying</u> on the bus for her commute. It was already past 7 PM when she stepped off the bus, cold and soaked to the bone, ③<u>having left</u> her umbrella at the gym. Her legs moved on their own, and suddenly, the Cups & Blossoms' bell was ④<u>ringing</u> above her head. She was also polite enough not to ask why Vera looked so tired, which was ⑤<u>appreciating</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: "which was appreciated"에서 주어(it)가 감사히 여겨지는 대상이므로 수동태(was appreciated)가 필요하다.
det.analysis:
❌⑤appreciating: which was appreciated → 수동태 필요
✅①couldn't: 조동사 부정
✅②relying: mean + ~ing(~을 의미하다)
✅③having left: 완료 분사구문
✅④ringing: 진행형(was ringing)
det.tip: which was appreciated = 그것은 감사히 여겨졌다 (수동태)

questions.passage: It was the day I had been ①<u>preparing</u> for. I drove for an hour and a half to apply for a visa. That same day, I helped three people who didn't know English by ②<u>translating</u> for the immigration officer. Believing things were going ③<u>smoothly</u>, I made my way to the counter. Unfortunately, the officer, who had smiled when I was helping her, suddenly turned ④<u>serious</u>. I didn't expect to hear her words of ⑤<u>acceptance</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 빨간 도장, 서류 무시 등 거절 상황이므로 rejection(거절)이 적절. acceptance(수락)는 맥락에 맞지 않음.
det.analysis:
❌⑤acceptance(수락): 원문은 rejection(거절). 빨간 도장+서류 무시=거절 상황
✅①preparing ✅②translating ✅③smoothly ✅④serious
det.tip: rejection(거절) ↔ acceptance(수락)

questions.passage: The group members were all ①<u>experienced</u>, so I couldn't understand why they were climbing so slowly — what I thought was a ②<u>ridiculous</u> pace. And, being the rookie, I wanted to prove myself to the group. Why not show off my ③<u>superior</u> conditioning? In a matter of minutes, I became a basket case, needing ④<u>assistance</u> just to walk. Now all I felt was ⑤<u>reward</u> for becoming a burden to the group.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 짐이 된 것에 대해 죄책감(guilt)을 느끼는 것이 자연스러움. reward(보상)는 맥락에 맞지 않음.
det.analysis:
❌⑤reward(보상): 원문은 guilt(죄책감). 짐이 된 것에 보상을 느끼는 것은 부적절
✅①experienced ✅②ridiculous ✅③superior ✅④assistance
det.tip: guilt(죄책감) ↔ reward(보상)

det.korean: 가장 소중한 소유물(possession). 오르간은 악기이지만 여기서는 "가장 소중한 소유물"로서 위안과 기쁨의 원천으로 표현됨.
det.analysis:
✅③possession(소유물): 가장 소중한 소유물
❌①instrument(악기): 의미는 통하나 precious와의 조합이 부자연스러움
❌②decoration(장식): 오르간은 장식이 아님
❌④weapon(무기): 문맥과 무관
❌⑤melody(멜로디): 오르간 자체가 멜로디는 아님
det.tip: possession = 소유물 / precious possession = 소중한 소유물

det.korean: whisper → Whispering: 분사구문, 능동/동시동작. 속삭이면서 이끌었다.
det.analysis: Whispering: 분사구문(능동/동시동작) → 현재분사
det.tip: 분사구문: 주어 동일 + 능동 → 현재분사(V-ing)

questions.passage: Consumer surveys indicate that the majority of Americans (91%) believe they have some control over their health, and 72% believe that food and nutrition play the greatest role. However, 75% of consumers rely on media outlets including the Internet as their major sources of health and nutrition information, and only half use medical sources. A Google search for “nutrition listservs” yielded over 100,000 sites, but it is likely that many of these writings are not reviewed by nutrition experts. Internet sites marketing herbs, drugs, and health devices are not monitored by government regulatory agencies and often contain misleading information. Reputable food companies provide helpful facts about the nutrient content of their products, but commercial sites devoted to sales often post misleading health claims. Internet sites maintained by government agencies, universities, state extension services, and medical facilities provide evidence-based information and should be the first source for public information on foods, nutrition, and health.

det.korean: "because of the nausea, headache, and dizziness" → 메스꺼움, 두통, 어지러움
det.analysis: nausea(메스꺼움), headache(두통), dizziness(어지러움) — 본문에서 직접 확인 가능
det.tip: because of 뒤에 나열된 세 가지 증상을 찾기
